title: Aid to least developed countries
description: ODA to the least developed countries as a share of each donor's total.
content: Each line is one donor's share over time. A rising line means the donor sends a larger part of its aid to the poorest countries.

title: Concessional lending by the World Bank
description: Loans and grants from the International Development Association, by region.
content: IDA commitments peaked in 2022, during the pandemic response. Commitments are what the Bank agrees to lend in the fiscal year, whether or not it pays out.

title: Remittances to low- and middle-income countries
description: Money migrants send home, as the World Bank estimates it.
content: Remittances reached USD 656 billion in 2023, more than ODA and foreign direct investment together.

title: Remittances and other flows
description: Remittances, ODA and foreign direct investment to low- and middle-income countries, in current US dollars.
content: The chart shows the latest year each source reports. The three series come from different sources, so their latest years can differ.

title: Debt service, change since 2015
description: How much more or less each country pays in external debt service than in 2015.
content: Zambia's payments fell after its default in 2020. Kenya's have more than tripled.

title: Debt service compared with 2015
description: Each bar is the change in a country's external debt service from its 2015 level, in percent.
content: Bars to the right mean a country pays more than in 2015. The series starts in 2015 because that is the first year the source covers every country.

title: ODA fell 7% in 2024
description: Net ODA from DAC members, in constant prices.
content: The drop followed cuts by France, Germany and the United Kingdom.

title: ODA from DAC members, 2000 to 2024
description: Net ODA from DAC members each year since 2000, in constant prices.
content: From 2018 the OECD counts loans at their grant equivalent, so earlier years use a different method. The break is marked on the axis.

title: Three donors gave half of all climate finance
description: Climate finance by provider, as reported to the UNFCCC.
content: Providers report under the UNFCCC's common tabular format. Multilateral finance is attributed to the providers that fund the institutions.

title: Climate finance by provider
description: Climate finance by provider, as reported to the UNFCCC.
content: The common tabular format was adopted in 2018 and first used for the 2021 reports. Before then providers used their own tables, so totals before 2021 are less comparable.

title: Arrears on external debt
description: Overdue payments of principal and interest on external public debt.
content: Arrears hit a record in 2022, as several countries stopped paying while they restructured. Arrears count only payments past their due date.

title: Arrears, explained
description: What counts as an arrear on external public debt.
content: A payment is in arrears from the day after it falls due. A country that restructures its debt can clear its arrears, and the new terms then apply.

title: Sudan's humanitarian funding
description: Humanitarian funding to Sudan against what the UN appeal asked for.
content: The 2024 appeal was less than half funded by the end of the year. Funding turned down after 2021, when donor attention moved to Ukraine.

title: Humanitarian appeals and funding
description: Each UN appeal's requirement and the funding it received, by year.
content: The grey bar is what the appeal asked for, and the blue bar is what donors gave. An appeal runs for one calendar year.

title: Gavi's funding, 2021 to 2025
description: Pledges to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, for its strategy period.
content: Pledges for 2026 to 2030 came in below the alliance's target of USD 11.9 billion. Each strategy period covers five years of vaccine programmes.
